The checker matched the word "input", which appeared in my comments ("input pair"). I removed that word, renamed the related comments and variables, and dropped the `try/except` blocks so the forbidden-construct scan passes. The circuit itself is the same StrongARM latch as before: tail switch, differential pair, cross-coupled latch, four PMOS reset switches and output inverters.

```python
PARAMS = {
    "W_in":   (3.0, 1.0, 8.0),    # differential pair width [um], L=0.15
    "W_tail": (2.0, 0.8, 6.0),    # clocked tail switch width [um]
    "W_ln":   (1.0, 0.42, 3.0),   # latch NMOS width
    "W_lp":   (1.0, 0.42, 3.0),   # latch PMOS width
    "W_rst":  (0.6, 0.42, 2.0),   # reset PMOS width
    "W_on":   (1.0, 0.42, 3.0),   # output inverter NMOS
    "W_op":   (2.0, 0.42, 6.0),   # output inverter PMOS
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    L = 0.15
    vdd = 1.8
    cl = spec.get("cl", 10e-15)
    dv = spec.get("dv", 0.002)

    n = Netlist("vinp vinn clk outp outn vdd vss")
    # tail switch
    n.M("M0", "tail", "clk", "vss", "vss", "nfet", p["W_tail"], L)
    # differential pair: vinp higher -> p1 (then dn) discharges faster
    n.M("M1", "p1", "vinp", "tail", "vss", "nfet", p["W_in"], L)
    n.M("M2", "p2", "vinn", "tail", "vss", "nfet", p["W_in"], L)
    # cross-coupled latch
    n.M("M3", "dn", "dp", "p1", "vss", "nfet", p["W_ln"], L)
    n.M("M4", "dp", "dn", "p2", "vss", "nfet", p["W_ln"], L)
    n.M("M5", "dn", "dp", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_lp"], L)
    n.M("M6", "dp", "dn", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_lp"], L)
    # reset switches (clk low = reset)
    n.M("MR1", "dn", "clk", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_rst"], L)
    n.M("MR2", "dp", "clk", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_rst"], L)
    n.M("MR3", "p1", "clk", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_rst"], L)
    n.M("MR4", "p2", "clk", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_rst"], L)
    # output inverters: dn falls -> outp rises
    n.M("MI1", "outp", "dn", "vss", "vss", "nfet", p["W_on"], L)
    n.M("MI2", "outp", "dn", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_op"], L)
    n.M("MI3", "outn", "dp", "vss", "vss", "nfet", p["W_on"], L)
    n.M("MI4", "outn", "dp", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_op"], L)

    # ---- first-order predictions ----
    cpu = 1.6e-15   # approx gate+overlap+junction cap per um width at L=0.15
    it = max(lut.op("n", p["W_tail"], L, vdd, 0.3)["Id"], 1e-5)
    gm_pair = 10.0 * it / 2           # assume gm/Id ~10 during integration
    c_p = cpu * (p["W_in"] + p["W_ln"] + p["W_rst"])
    c_d = cpu * (p["W_ln"] + p["W_lp"] + p["W_rst"] + p["W_on"] + p["W_op"]) \
        + cpu * (p["W_ln"] + p["W_lp"])
    # integration: p and d nodes drop ~one Vth (~0.6 V)
    t_int = (c_p + c_d) * 0.6 / (it / 2)
    av = gm_pair * 0.6 / (it / 2)
    # regeneration
    gml = lut.op("n", p["W_ln"], L, 0.9, 0.9)["gm"] + lut.op("p", p["W_lp"], L, 0.9, 0.9)["gm"]
    tau = c_d / max(gml, 1e-6)
    t_reg = tau * math.log(max(vdd / (2 * av * dv), 2.0))
    t_inv = 0.69 * cl / (300e-6 * p["W_op"] / 2.5 + 1e-9) * 0.5
    delay = t_int + t_reg + t_inv + 15e-12

    # energy: four internal nodes recharged, one output toggles, plus clock gates
    c_int = 2 * c_p + 2 * c_d
    c_out = cl + cpu * (p["W_on"] + p["W_op"])
    c_clk = cpu * (p["W_tail"] + 4 * p["W_rst"])
    energy = (c_int + c_out + 0.5 * c_clk) * vdd ** 2

    return n, {"correct": 1, "delay": delay, "energy": energy}
```
